claims.statement: The GPSR applies since 13 December 2024, requires an EU-established responsible person for covered products and requires specified manufacturer, responsible-person, product-identification, warning and safety information in distance-sale offers.
Safety Gate validated 4,671 alerts and 5,794 follow-up actions in 2025, and its public alerts can be integrated into business and marketplace processes.
The Commission permits reuse of published Safety Gate alerts when meaning is not distorted and the required attribution is preserved, so the core alert feed is usable but not proprietary.
eBay, Shopify and Etsy already provide native listing fields or bulk workflows for GPSR manufacturer, economic-operator and safety information.
eBay states that listings missing required GPSR information may be hidden from or made unpurchasable by EU and Northern Ireland buyers, evidencing a concrete merchant trigger.

General feed management and GPSR record tools are publicly offered at low monthly prices, including Channable from EUR 59 per month for 5,000 items and a Shopify GPSR app up to USD 79.99 per month for unlimited products and API access.
Not every business-submitted Safety Gate field is published, including manufacturer-identification fields described in the official manual, which can make automated recall-to-SKU matching incomplete.

A software syndicator may prepare and transmit evidence under merchant authorization, but the responsible economic operator retains the underlying product-safety duties and a model should not represent unverified documents as legal certification.

contrary_evidence: Major commerce platforms already expose native GPSR fields, and eBay supports individual and bulk updates.
Channable handles large multi-channel catalogs from EUR 59 per month and a GPSR Shopify app offers unlimited-product API access for USD 79.99 per month, pressuring per-SKU pricing.
Safety Gate alerts are public and reusable with attribution, so the raw alert corpus is not a data moat.
Some Safety Business Gateway fields are not published, making exact recall matching harder and increasing false-positive risk.
Etsy already directs sellers to responsible-person partners, and native marketplace or feed vendors can extend into document verification.
Low-SKU merchants can comply manually or exit EEA sales rather than buy another system.

economics.acquisition_route: UNVALIDATED: sell directly to responsible-person firms serving one selected product category and let the partner distribute the workflow across its merchant base. No partner commitment, conversion rate, exclusivity or channel economics is asserted.
economics.capital_required_pln: No new amount is asserted. The one-category, partner-operated scope avoids a broad connector build and must be tested within the founder's disclosed 100000 PLN available capital; legal, integration, insurance and support costs remain unknown.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: No defensible timeline or valuation is asserted. A path to the founder's 5 million PLN target requires repeatable partner economics across enough responsible-person firms, positive contribution after support, durable renewal and retained founder ownership; all remain unvalidated.
economics.founder_time: UNVALIDATED: the software and partner-enablement scope is intended to fit the founder's 5-hour daily ceiling because qualified partner staff perform document and incident review; actual integration, support and sales load is unmeasured.
economics.gross_margin_basis: No margin percentage is asserted. Direct costs are extraction, provenance storage, category-rule maintenance, partner integrations and support; the responsible-person firm supplies qualified review and merchant service under the design.
economics.payback: No acquisition-payback or customer-payback period is asserted. It depends on partner acquisition cost, accepted-dossier volume, reduced intake and incident labor, listing continuity and partner renewal.
economics.pricing: UNVALIDATED MODEL ONLY: an annual partner-workspace license plus usage tied to accepted dossier/onboarding and human-reviewed incident workflows; no amount is asserted until paid discovery establishes willingness to pay.
economics.retention_or_repeat: No retention rate is asserted. Repeat depends on embedding in the partner's intake gate, recurring dossier maintenance, incident handling and proven labor or listing-continuity value.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: partner-owned category-specific corpus of resolved evidence deficiencies, reviewer decisions and confirmed product identifiers that improves its intake templates; reuse across merchants occurs only when authorized
fingerprint.customer: EU responsible-person firms serving importers and marketplace sellers in one selected high-risk consumer-product category
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: direct embedding through a responsible-person firm that already serves merchants in the selected category; the partner owns merchant acquisition, specialist review and channel delivery, with no exclusive or preferred agreement assumed
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: category-specific intake and acceptance workflow with provenance checks, reviewer queues, approved channel-ready records and human-confirmed incident routing; not a horizontal field store, legal certification or automatic takedown
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the responsible-person firm pays for an internal workspace and accepted dossier/onboarding and human-reviewed incident workflows; no price or commitment is assumed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a responsible-person firm must decide whether to accept and maintain a merchant's product evidence, publish approved GPSR data across channels, or review a suspected Safety Gate match

founder_fit: Strong fit with entity resolution, provenance, data pipelines and audit automation, without camera exposure or a personal brand.
A one-category partner-operated product is intended to fit the founder's 5-hour daily ceiling and disclosed capital, but integration and support effort remain unknown.
The responsible-person firm supplies product-safety expertise, merchant acquisition and incident judgment, avoiding a non-delegable specialist role for the founder.
Concentrated partner distribution reduces high-energy direct merchant sales but creates dependence on a small number of firms whose willingness to embed the workflow is unvalidated.

redesign.economic_effect: Moves the payer from high-SKU merchants to an embedded responsible-person firm and the usage unit from active SKUs to accepted dossier/onboarding and reviewed-incident events. Qualified review, merchant acquisition and channel delivery shift to the partner, reducing direct price competition with field tools and founder labor, while leaving willingness to pay, price, margin, volume and partner commitment unproven.

risks: Responsible-person firms may reject, build or bundle the workflow, and a concentrated partner channel can create severe dependency.
Supplier evidence may be forged, stale or inconsistent, and the software must not present reviewer-approved records as legal certification.
Incomplete public alert identifiers can still create false matches or missed products; every incident action requires qualified human review.
A partner may expect the founder to assume specialist judgment, liability or continuous incident operations despite the intended role boundary.
Marketplace APIs and GPSR fields can change, remain inaccessible or be better served by low-cost native and feed tools.
Cross-merchant reuse of evidence and match outcomes may be contractually restricted, weakening the learning advantage.
The selected category may have too little volume or too much expert-review cost to support positive contribution economics.

structure.commercial_archetype: agency-embedded vertical operations software tied to dossier acceptance and incident review
structure.control_point: the responsible-person firm's merchant and product dossier acceptance gate, before approved data is released to commerce channels
structure.critical_dependency: a responsible-person firm choosing to embed the workflow, qualified reviewers, merchant-authorized evidence access and sufficiently identifying public alert data

thesis: Embed a category-specific evidence-intake and incident workflow inside EU responsible-person firms rather than sell merchants a horizontal GPSR field-and-alert tool. For one selected product category, the partner uses the system at the point where it accepts and maintains a merchant's product dossier: it checks provenance, maps approved data into channel-ready records, records reviewer decisions and routes ambiguous public Safety Gate matches to a qualified human reviewer. The responsible-person firm, not the founder, performs specialist review and owns the merchant relationship; the software never certifies safety or automatically removes a listing. The payer and unit of sale change from per-SKU merchant charges to a partner workspace plus accepted dossier/onboarding and reviewed-incident events, avoiding direct competition with cheap native fields and feed transport. Demand, partner commitment, category economics, access rights and accuracy remain unknown.
title: Category-Specific Responsible-Person Evidence Operations System
uncertainties: Paid willingness and implementation commitment from a responsible-person firm.
Which product category combines enough dossier and incident volume with manageable specialist-review cost.
Merchant-authorized access and complete channel-field mappings for the first partner's workflows.
Measured document-review cost, alert-match precision and recall, and reduction in intake or incident labor.
Permission to reuse resolved evidence patterns and confirmed identifiers across merchant accounts.
Partner acquisition cost, pricing, contribution margin, renewal, concentration and founder-compatible support load.
